question: In which year was the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) in India formed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2005**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA)** was established in **2005** under the aegis of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India. 
• The primary purpose of NADA is to promote **clean sport** and ensure the integrity of athletes by preventing the use of **performance-enhancing drugs**. 
• NADA operates in accordance with the **World Anti-Doping Code**, which is a set of global standards for anti-doping measures created by the **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)**. 
• The agency is responsible for conducting **dope testing**, educating athletes about anti-doping rules, and implementing awareness programs. 
• NADA's jurisdiction includes **domestic athletes** and events, ensuring compliance with anti-doping regulations at the **national level**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Functions of NADA:** 
• **Testing and Investigation**: NADA conducts doping tests during competitions and outside of competitions to ensure adherence to anti-doping rules. 
• **Education and Awareness**: The agency organizes workshops, seminars, and campaigns to educate athletes, coaches, and support staff about the consequences of doping. 
• **Results Management**: NADA handles the process of analyzing test results and taking necessary disciplinary actions against those found guilty of doping violations. 
• **Coordination with WADA**: NADA ensures compliance with international anti-doping standards and collaborates with WADA for global anti-doping efforts. 
• **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA):** 
• WADA was established in **1999** as an independent agency to combat doping in sports worldwide. 
• The agency introduced the **World Anti-Doping Code** to unify anti-doping policies globally. 
• WADA's headquarters are located in **Montreal, Canada**, and it oversees compliance for all national anti-doping organizations. 
• **Significant Achievements of NADA:** 
• NADA has successfully conducted **thousands of doping tests** and implemented stringent measures for ensuring fair play in sports. 
• The agency actively collaborates with international bodies like **WADA** and regional anti-doping organizations to enhance its capabilities. 
• It has played a critical role in preventing doping scandals and maintaining India's reputation in the global sports arena. 
• **Anti-Doping Rules in India:** 
• The **Anti-Doping Rules, 2021** were introduced to align with WADA's **2021 Code** and improve the enforcement of anti-doping measures. 
• These rules cover various aspects, including **testing protocols, prohibited substances, therapeutic use exemptions (TUEs)**, and penalties for violations. 
• They emphasize the importance of **athlete education** and aim to create a doping-free sports culture. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Prohibited Substances:** 
• NADA publishes a **list of prohibited substances and methods** annually, which is based on WADA's guidelines. 
• Substances like **anabolic steroids, stimulants, narcotics**, and masking agents are banned for athletes. 
• **Consequences of Doping:** 
• Athletes found guilty of doping face **sanctions**, including **disqualification, suspension, fines**, and lifetime bans depending on the severity of the violation. 
• Repeated violations can lead to harsher penalties and loss of reputation in the sports community. 
• **Role of Athletes:** 
• Athletes are required to stay updated on anti-doping regulations and avoid using prohibited substances. 
• They must ensure compliance with testing protocols and cooperate with NADA during investigations. </ul
